title: Why laws change

match.reason: None of the bank points explains why laws change; the closest, Agents of change, covers social change in general from a Society and Culture course rather than the three reasons for law reform in this point, so a new point is the right fit.

draft.title: Why laws change
card: Laws are not fixed. Parliament and the courts can change them when they stop suiting the community.
what people think is acceptable can shift over time. Laws may then be changed to match the new view.
inventions can create situations that old laws never planned for. New or updated laws may be needed to cover them.
A law that no longer works
a law may be unclear, hard to enforce or fail to achieve its purpose. It may then be reformed or repealed (removed).
draft.remember: Laws change to keep up with the community, with new technology and with what works.

a.q: Which situation is the best example of a law changing because of new technology?
opts: Parliament creates an offence for misusing drones in crowds
Parliament lowers a penalty after public attitudes soften
Parliament repeals a law that police could not enforce
Parliament rewrites an unclear law that courts dispute
a.why: Drones are a new invention that older laws did not plan for, so a new offence was needed. The option about softer attitudes shows changing values, not technology.
a.clue: Look for the option where a new invention creates the need.

b.q: A Victorian law bans an activity, but police rarely charge anyone because the wording is vague and courts keep dismissing cases. Which reason for change does this show best?
opts: The community wants a harsher penalty
b.why: The law is failing in practice because it is unclear and hard to enforce. Nothing in the case says attitudes changed, so changing values is the tempting but wrong choice.
b.clue: Ask whether the problem is the community, a new invention, or the law itself.

a.best: Parliament creates an offence for misusing drones in crowds
